sentences.text:
This is the second application filed by the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to FIR No. 103/2023 registered at P.S - MIG,
Indore , District-Indore (M.P.) for the offence under sections 420, 406 of IPC 2/

As per prosecution story on 16/02/2023, complainant Deepak Bhandari lodged FIR at police station - MIG, Indore by stating that about three years ago, an agreement to sale was executed between the complainant and the applicant and as per the agreement, the complainant paid Rs. 1,80,000/- to the applicant through cheque and Rs. 1,00,000/- by cash, but the applicant did not execute the registered sale deed in favour of the complainant.
Actually, the applicant is not the owner of the said plot and committed cheating with the complainant, hence the aforementioned offence has been registered against the applicant.

3/ Learned counsel for the applicant contended that the applicant is an innocent person and has Rajesh Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139102395/
1 been falsely implicated in the instant case.

sentences.text: The matter has been amicably settled between the parties.
No dispute has remained between them.
They have executed compromise deed.
He is permanent resident of District- Indore
Under these circumstances, he prays that present applicant be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4/ Per-contra, learned GA has opposed the application and prays for its rejection by stating that one criminal antecedent has been found against the applicant.

5/. Although nobody appeared on behalf of the complainant, but the complainant has filed his affidavit along with compromise deed by stating that the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties and no dispute has remained between them, hence he has no objection, if the applicant is granted anticipatory bail.
6/- Perused the case diary as well as impugned order passed by the trial Court.

7/ Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature allegation and taking note of the fact that after registration of the FIR, the matter has been amicably settled between the complainant and the applicant; the complainant pleaded no objection, if the applicant is granted anticipatory bail; in view of the material evidence available on record, I deem it proper to allow the present application.
8/ Accordingly, without commenting upon the merits of the case, present application for grant of anticipatory bail is hereby allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rs. Seventy FiveThousand) along with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of arresting officer for his appearance before the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation as and when directed.
9/ However, all the conditions of Section 438(2) Cr.P.C. shall also apply on the applicant during currency of bail.
10/ With the aforesaid, the application stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per rules.
